So here we have a spider whose venom causes frostbite. There is another SCP object with a similar effect to be found in SCP-2082, in which we have a extinct species of mammoth that cause the surrounding environment to drop in temperature. You could say these effects are scaled to the size of the creature. As such, it may be possible that what ever gave 2082 its powers may now be effecting 548. As such, I am proposing the following additional addendum:

Addendum 2: It is possible that the same anomalous effect that was historically responsible for SCP-2082 may now be effecting SCP-548. Research into this link is currently underway using SCP-2082 tissue samples preserved following Incident 2082-Prime. Proposals to resume the SCP-2082 cloning program for use of a live specimen have been denied.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.content:encoded: This thing injects half a milliliter of venom, which is enough to freeze a human limb solid. Either that is one hell of an endothermic reaction, or there's something anomalous going on… and even if the chemistry itself isn't anomalous, whatever process permits a living arachnid to produce such a freaky-ass venom certainly is.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I'm kind of wondering why this isn't an EX-SCP. Sure, it's unheard of, but isn't it scientifically explainable? The venom is a liquid that undergoes an extreme endothermic reaction on contact with the air, and there are other creatures that can survive being frozen with no ill effects (i.e. cockroaches, tardigrades).

I guess I'm saying that the only really anomalous thing about this SCP is that it doesn't seem to have come from any sort of evolutionary progression - that it seems to have just come out of nowhere; and while all the genetic mutations it would take to make this kind of tarantula happening all at once in one embryo is extremely unlikely, it's not quite impossible, is it? If it's completely scientifically explainable, it's not an SCP…right? Am I missing something here?
